chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about a man who died leaving young and adult sons and daughters, without a will, and he had servants and female slaves and debts. How should the heirs manage the division of that inheritance? He said, 'If a trustworthy man stands among them and divides all of it for them, there is no harm.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khurasani wrote: In the case of a man who left an heir to a man, and he had paternal cousins, daughters of paternal cousins, a paternal uncle, and two paternal aunts, to whom is the inheritance? He (peace be upon him) wrote back, 'The people of the 'asabah (agnates), the paternal cousins, they are the heirs.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is a narration consistent with the general public (Sunni), but we do not adopt it because we have clarified that the nearer in lineage is more entitled to inheritance. And if that is established, then in this case the inheritance belongs to the two paternal aunts, because they are nearer than the children of the paternal uncle and the paternal uncle.

key_terms.الْأَقْرَبَ فَالْأَقْرَبَ: The nearer is more entitled (principle of proximity in inheritance)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia inheritance law differ from Sunni law regarding paternal aunts versus paternal cousins?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia principle of *al-aqrab fa al-aqrab* (the nearer in kinship is more entitled), contrasting it with the Sunni practice of *al-awla bil-awla* (priority to the closest male). The text explicitly notes that while the cousin scenario aligns with the general consensus (*muwafiq lil-'amma*), Shia jurists reject it in favor of closer female relatives like paternal aunts, demonstrating the flexibility of Shia inheritance law in excluding males when females are nearer. This reflects the broader Shia methodology of prioritizing direct proximity over gender in certain branches of inheritance.
